core_obligations: Identify the degreewise sequence: the sheaf condition says that the kernel of (1, -1) : F(U) plus F(V) -> F(U cap V) is the image of F(X), for any abelian sheaf; and the restriction lemma shows that (1, -1) is surjective on sections of an injective module (proof lines 782-788).

Build a short exact sequence of complexes: applying the two facts degree by degree to an injective resolution F -> I^bullet yields the short exact sequence 0 -> I^bullet(X) -> I^bullet(U) plus I^bullet(V) -> I^bullet(U cap V) -> 0 of complexes (proof lines 789-797).
Conclude: taking cohomology of that short exact sequence of complexes gives the displayed long exact sequence; the author leaves the functoriality in F unproved (proof lines 798-800).
proof_roadmap: Use the sheaf condition for the kernel and the injective-restriction lemma for the surjectivity, both degreewise in an injective resolution (proof lines 782-788).
Package these into a short exact sequence of complexes of sections over X, U, V and U cap V (proof lines 789-797).
Take the long exact cohomology sequence of that short exact sequence to obtain the displayed sequence (proof lines 798-800).
difficulty_reason: The lemma produces the Mayer-Vietoris long exact sequence 0 -> H^0(X, F) -> H^0(U, F) plus H^0(V, F) -> H^0(U cap V, F) -> H^1(X, F) -> ... for a ringed space covered by two open subsets, with functoriality in F (statement lines 768-778). The proof does not chase the sequence directly; it assembles a short exact sequence of complexes of sections of an injective resolution, where the two required properties come from different places: the kernel part is the sheaf condition, and the surjectivity part is the separate lemma that restriction of an injective module to an open is surjective (proof lines 782-797). The author explicitly leaves the functoriality unproved, and that sentence is reproduced as written. The claim is H2: one assembly of two cited facts into an exact sequence of complexes.
